question.problem: What is ${\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{k}=a+kΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)={x}^{5},$ the lower bound is $a=1$ and the upper bound is $b=2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{2-1}{n}=\frac{1}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}f({x}_{k})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(1+k\cdot \frac{1}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[f(1+\frac{k}{n})\cdot \frac{1}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{k=1}^{n}[{(1+\frac{k}{n})}^{5}\cdot \frac{1}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
